title: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth's State of the Force Address (As Delivered)
text: Warriors, good afternoon. One year ago today, I stood right here, on this very stage, and addressed Generals, and Admirals, and Sergeants Major. Now, the hyperventilating media thought it might be an impromptu PT test. Maybe it should have been. Instead, the speech was a declaration of independence for the War Department. Marking a clean break from the Defense Department of old. The speech reestablished a singular mission for the department: warfighting. Preparing to fight — and preparing to win. Unrelenting, unapologetic, and uncompromising in that single pursuit. Now, I think the Generals heard the message. Those who responded positively — which is most of them — are leading newly focused, and newly empowered, and disciplined formations. Those generals who did not — who clung to the "Woke Department" or seem to think civilian control of the military is simply a suggestion, well, they no longer work here. You see, the number-crunchers say we fired 10% of the generals and admirals across the force, and that number sounds about right. And I know, because I directed it — that we've also reduced the overall number of general officer slots by an additional 10%. So, yes, 20% reduction across the board. Now the media calls that a "purge." I call it accountability and long overdue. And frankly, the bare minimum. As usual, what the media levels as an accusation, I wear as an accomplishment. You see, you can't change a culture with the same people who enabled it. Personnel is policy — at every single level. But today, I'm talking to an even more important group of Americans. The top E6s, Staff Sergeants, First Class Petty Officers, and Technical Sergeants, and top O3s. Captains and Navy Lieutenants across the entire military. E6s and O3s. Now it could have been E5s, or E7s, or O2s, or O4s. But I've got a sweet spot, a special thing for E6s and O3s and I'll share why later. The best of the best. You see, last year's speech was not for those Generals. It was for you. The backbone of our force. The current and future leaders on the front lines. Now, later in this speech, I'm going to make six brand new announcements that will transform the future of the force you serve in. Today's speech is entitled the "State of the Force" and it is intended to be a new annual tradition where the Secretary gives an update and casts the vision for the future of the department. Now for almost two years, you've heard me talk over and over and over about three core priorities: reviving the warrior ethos; rebuilding the military; and reestablishing deterrence. And I'm proud to stand on this stage and report that the warrior ethos has been revived. Our military is being rebuilt. And American deterrence is back. Simply put, thanks to the courageous and common-sense leadership of our Commander-in-Chief, President Donald J. Trump, the state of our Force today is stronger than it has ever been in our Nation's history. I'm looking out at the most capable, the most focused, and the most lethal in American history. You see, I'd like to think that last year's Quantico speech was Liberation Day for leaders. For you to be the apolitical, hard-charging, common-sense, no-nonsense Constitutional leaders you joined the military to be. You see, this stuff is not rocket-science. But it is a revival. The power is back in the hands of Commanders and NCOs. Not lawyers and HR reps. Telling someone to get in shape, or shave, or fix their uniform, or start busting their ass — that's not discrimination. That's leadership. We have ended the poisonous culture of risk aversion and empowered leaders at every single level to simply enforce standards. The only focus, as you know in your formations, should be training, readiness, accountability, discipline, and lethality. And when you pursue those things, you don't have to walk on eggshells. No more social engineering. No more weaponized IG policies — the complainers, the ideologues, and the poor performers are no longer in the driver's seat. No more silly PowerPoint trainings or drag queen shows. No more diversity quotas, no more gender pronouns, no more identity months. Only the warrior ethos. And I know you feel it, because I've been to your units and met with your troops. It has transformed entire formations as it was intended to do. But it's worth saying again, so that the Fake News understands it. We are no longer the Woke Department or the Weak Department. Simple translation of that: No fatties. No trannies. No beardos. No weirdos. No wimps. No radicals. Just warriors. Just tough, ready, committed troops. The War Department, as you know, is color-blind, gender-neutral, and merit-based. Or as the President says to me, "Pete … central casting. I want central casting." The ideological clowns are out. The patriotic cowboys are in — with testosterone testing on top. Diversity is not our strength, unity is our strength. Because that's all that really matters when the missiles are flying. The delusional media will downplay all the progress of the past year, but this group — right here — and I look forward to hearing from you all tomorrow morning as well — knows how real and how important culture change is has been. But allow me to digress, briefly, to address that delusional media. You're all here, and I'm here to talk to you but for a moment I'm going to talk to them and through them. To the fake news. To start, there's a few headlines that they could run that they just haven't gotten to. Guess what? In today's War Department, military sexual assaults are down. In today's War Department, military suicides are down. In today's War Department, Black and female recruitment are up, even though all quotas are gone. Hmm, shocking. How could that be? Quite an inconvenient truth that doesn't quite fit their narrative, does it? Not only is our force more ready and lethal, but it's healthier than ever. Color-blind, gender-neutral, merit based. Everyone, of all shades, loves that. Instead, you read disingenuous headlines about deployment lengths, patently false claims of low troop morale, or flat-out propaganda as if it's written by our adversaries — and frankly, sometimes it is. Take Iran, for example. Allow me to lay it out simply for the anti-American losers in our media: these Americans, right here, and their peers, these — have destroyed Iran's Navy, destroyed Iran's Air Force, destroyed their air defense systems, their leadership, and their military industrial capacity. Their entire defense base. Iran's conventional shield has been crippled, and their nuclear ambitions laid bare for the world. You, this group, are ensuring that Iran never gets a nuclear weapon. Courageous and historic operations that every red-blooded American is proud of. But, as you know, the information space … it's a battle space. Yet our so-called press makes Iranian state media look reasonable. Our media's shameful lust for political retribution blinds them to the consequences of reckless, so-called reporting. So-called journalists, juiced up on Trump derangement syndrome, think they're fighting against our President, but they're really undermining you, our warfighters. Bottom line: too many of them hate the President more than they love the country. You see, it's your movements and bases that they reveal to the enemy. It's your operations they jeopardize when they leak classified capabilities. And ultimately, it's your lives they put directly at risk when they lie about munitions stockpiles. All for a banner that will scroll on TV for 30 seconds. And I know a little bit about banners scrolling on TV for 30 seconds. A free press is of course important, but partisan activism that intentionally smears the troops and the historic mission they are undertaking is fundamentally anti-American. It's sick. It's a national betrayal. It's treason, actually. I hate to have to say it, but it has to be said, especially in defense of the great Americans right in front of me. But you, nonetheless, continue forward. Because you love the country more than they can fathom. The haters, as just I illustrated, don't understand the stakes of your profession. But you do. Which is why, one year ago, we launched three leadership litmus tests, some of which I talked about this morning, that we live by every day in this department. The War Department Golden Rule, the 1990 Test, and the E6/O3 Test. First, and most importantly, the Golden Rule. My sons, all my kids, are no more important than yours. All precious souls, made in the image and likeness of God. Every parent in this country deserves to know that their child that joins our ranks is entering exactly the kind of unit that the Secretary of War would want his son to join. Jesus said, and you know it, "Do unto others as you would have done unto yourself." It is the simplest test of truth. Well, the new War Department Golden Rule that we put into practice is this: Do unto your unit as you would have done unto your own child's unit. Would you want them serving in a unit where standards were lowered to meet quotas? Or a unit where leaders were promoted for reasons other than merit, performance, or warfighting? The answer is not just no, the answer is hell no. We live this Golden Rule now, and standards have responded accordingly. And that means, for every combat MOS, none of this should be new to you because we've been doing this over the past year, we now have gender neutral standards set at the highest, male standard only. Because combat doesn't care. That means, for every combat MOS, we now have a combat field test, again, set at the highest, male standard only. Because combat doesn't care. That means two PT tests every year for every unit, and the same for height and weight standards. And soon, in every Service, for those PT tests, and I'm looking at the Army guys here. Guys and gals. It's a PT test that can be done with only a stopwatch and a clipboard. Stay tuned. No more mobile gym needed. That means PT every duty day. At every level, from Corporal to Commandant. That means not treating combat arms and non-combat arms as the same thing. Both very important, but not the same. And that means basic training is back to … basic training. Drill sergeants being drill sergeants. The same goes for how we pick senior leaders. We got rid of the DEI-based, social, emotional evaluations known in the Army as B-CAP and C-CAP. You won't have to endure them. They were Milley and Austin specials. Intended to create politically correct quotas for race and gender. Under the guise of double-blind psychology assessments, the previous administration forced out so-called "toxic leaders" in favor of promoting risk-averse, get-along-to-go-along conformists. It was the true politicization of the military. Stupid, and dangerous. Instead, now, we have instituted a performance-based Joint Warfighter Evaluation. Every colonel who wants to be a general will have to pass, and excel, in a merit-based, performance-driven assessment of a commander's ability to solve complex military problems and win on the battlefield. All of you deserve senior leaders who know how to war-fight, who will employ you like the War Department, not the State Department. Who will think outside the box — bold and violent. The previous administration wanted politically correct generals. We only want the top performing generals. It's not just pass or fail; it's racked and stacked. One to end. The best move on, the worst do not. Common sense. We also apply the 1990 Test and the E6/03 Test. Standards that existed in say 1990 now once again apply today. We have restored dozens. Turns out we were right, standards over time had dropped for all the wrong reasons. And everything we do is in service of making your jobs — the jobs of E6s and O3s easier. The E6/03 Test. Because you're the ones that make everything happen. Now it turns out this turnaround, because that's what it is, it's a turnaround, is wildly popular both inside our ranks and with young Americans looking from the outside. Retention rates, and you all know this, meaning troops who are staying in are at record rates. Including over 80% of the force on the USS Abraham Lincoln, on their historic mission. And it's all merit based. Our best O3s and our best E6s are choosing to stay in — which says everything and sets the tone for the entire force. And recruiting for every branch has been record setting ever since President Trump won in November 2024. Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, Space Force, National Guard, Reserves, pilots, Special Forces — all setting decades-long recruiting records. You see, Americans want to serve when they are led by strong patriots, not by weak weirdos. It makes sense. And all of this matters because, you know why it matters, because it translates to the battlefield. Our enemies know we will act decisively. Our allies know it's time to step up. Drug cartels, the terrorist organizations of our hemisphere who previously run our hemisphere, are now on the run in our hemisphere courtesy of our new counter-cartel coalition, the A Triple C. You heard on the film right behind me, Maduro said, "I'm right here, come and get me." So we did. "F-A-F-O," in action. And from Midnight Hammer to Epic Fury, Iran will never, ever have a nuclear weapon. Peace through strength, deterrence in action on behalf of the American people. We will fight to win. Clear missions, full hearts, hands untied. That is all I ever wanted as a platoon leader, and it's all my E6 squad leaders ever wanted, back again to the E6-O3 Test. We let our leaders fight their formations, and then we have their backs. It's simple, yet you know in your business, that's incredibly powerful and liberating. In fact, the greatest compliment I have received in this job, by far, has come from battlefield commanders. From Rough Rider to Maduro to Epic Fury, commanders have told me point blank, over and over, and said the same to the Chairman, "We've never — in our 10, 20, even 30 years in service — felt this supported. With authorities, capabilities, and backing like never before." Unleashed. Our boys come home; the enemy does not. Whatever it takes. Ask Dude 44-Alpha and Dude 44-Bravo. Not only are we a new department however on the battlefield, but also in the halls of the Pentagon. That big ol' building you looked at this morning. We are rebuilding the military, but not at the speed of government, not at the speed of this town, or that town, wherever it is, but at the speed of business. We have thrown out the failed bureaucratic playbook, and replaced it with an unrelenting focus on speed, scale, and rapid innovation. We are in a war of attrition against the Pentagon bureaucracy every single day, and it is a war we intend to win. We have traversed the country in an Arsenal of Freedom Tour, igniting our Defense Industrial Base that was long ignored and President Trump has revived with American manufacturing. We are open for business as a department, but not just for the big prime contractors, but for the new nimble, innovative companies that had to fight their way into the department in the past. And the historic $1.5 Trillion dollar budget that the President demands, which we will deliver, will ensure we are equipped to win and fight every future fight. That's what we owe you. But the new money that we get, we'll spend it differently. Our great Deputy Secretary Steve Feinberg, he's here somewhere, a patriotic billionaire … there he is. He is a patriotic billionaire turnaround specialist. He is our secret weapon. He is cutting new deals that will revolutionize our department forever. Defense companies now have to spend their own money, imagine that, to expand their plants, factories, and manufacturing lines, in exchange for predictable multi-year deals that allow them to invest and plan, and save taxpayers billions of dollars. We are now getting weapons faster than ever before. For this reason, and many more, it is imperative that Congress pass a $350B reconciliation package for our warriors. President Trump has promised a generational investment in the War Department, and we are going to deliver. We must fund the future fight. That, I know, is imperative. We have the most powerful and most prepared military on the planet. Nobody can touch us. It's not even close. My job, your job, our job is to keep it that way. Which brings us to today's six announcements. Which taken together with historic efforts already underway like the Golden Dome for America, or the Golden Fleet to protect the seas, and the F-47, will ensure our military stays on top for generations to come. So … let's go. First, today at my direction, we are announcing the creation of Autonomous Warfare Command, or AutoWarCom. A new 4-star combatant command, with service-like authorities, built to scale autonomous and robotic capabilities across the Joint Force in the fastest peacetime shift in modern military history. Drone warfare, supercharged by SI-enabled targeting, is the biggest battlefield revolution in generations. You already know that. Yet when I was sworn in, the Department of Defense, there was scant urgency in this domain. That changed as soon as we took the helm. We immediately launched the Drone Dominance program that cut through red tape and moved authorities out of the Pentagon and place it with commands. And we established Task Force 401, led by Army Brigadier General Matt Ross, a phenomenal leader, now the leading counter-drone unit across the entire government. To accelerate purchasing and fielding of these technologies, we fused the Defense Innovation Unit, DIU, with a Direct Report Program Manager, called a "DRPM." That team has shipped thousands of autonomous systems, of drones, to the Middle East and around the world, delivering lethal capabilities and outcomes in days and weeks rather than months or years. That's the normal speed of the Pentagon … months or years. It is a good start, but it is certainly not enough. The pace of war is changing faster than the processes to support it. Cheap computing, Super Intelligence, and advanced commercial manufacturing have enabled the proliferation of low-cost, high precision strike. You see, for forty years, the United States relied on an expensive weapon that only — not only, but primarily — on expensive weapons that placed quality over quantity. Now that approach gave us a lot of enormous advantages, and we need to preserve those capabilities. But today we need both quality and quantity. The term you know is "high-low mix." An analogy is a thunderstorm. We need bolts of lightning, high, our existing high-end kill chains, capable of striking unexpectedly and decisively. We also need steady wind and rain. Mass drones and other autonomous attrittable systems that flip the cost exchange and impose unrelenting pressure on an adversary on the battlefield. Ukraine's lesson is not that one type of drone wins wars but rather the need for a purpose-built system that maximizes the ability to adapt. We will fuse procurement with operations at scale, and allow our warfighters, engineers, and entrepreneurs to learn, adapt, and rapidly iterate for any domain and their mission. And that is why I am directing an interim step as well. Today the unmanned systems DRPM becomes Project Agincourt. Project Agincourt. Now, the name means something. In 1415, many moons agon, the outnumbered English army defeated a numerically superior French force in their legacy armor with a new technology — the long bow. The English had to look outside their traditional recruitment pools to find skilled archers. Now to maximize the rate of fire you need to be effective, they integrated fletchers, the craftsmen who made and repaired the arrows for the longbows. And they moved them close to the front lines to sustain the rate of fire. We face a very similar moment. Project Agincourt is not just a procurement vehicle. It is applying our commercial-first Drone Dominance playbook with DIU. Now it gets two brief additional missions. First, it will prototype a new construct called Warfighting Acquisition. Not just acquisition that happens at the Pentagon. This model fuses operators with entrepreneurs in rapid adaptation cycles, while distributing decisions and dollars closer to frontline units and the combatant commands. Realistic training exercises, and when possible, the crucible of combat, will be used to compress innovation timelines and scale what works. Now, this audience of any across the country understands why this formula unlocks advantage for the United States. You know the single greatest comparative advantage of the U.S. military is not a program, it is not a platform, and it certainly not a program office. It's our front-line combat leaders. By removing unnecessary layers, reducing the distance between our warfighters and our world-leading innovators, and then giving the right people the authority to act — Project Agincourt will pilot innovation at the edge, in a way that only Americans can do. And second, the culminating mission of Agincourt will take place over the course of months, clearing the path for Autonomous Warfare Command. The autonomous and robotic revolution has enormous implications for equipment, doctrine, organization, and the assumptions that have governed warfare for decades. Civilian leaders can provide direction and urgency, but lasting change must be anchored in military command structures and operationalized by leaders across our joint force. Now, any major institutional change like this one … it is a major institutional change, has always met resistance. Goldwater-Nichols faced opposition from the Secretary of Defense, the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs, and the military services. U.S. Special Operations Command, SOCOM, triggered a Pentagon revolt. Secretary of Defense Bob Gates had to fight his own building to fast-track MRAPs for the front lines. And President Trump's Space Force was opposed by the then-secretary, the Air Force, and the chairman. Yet, when the final order was given, the military executed and the force was better off as a result. Today I am giving a similar order, with the full support of President Trump. A man that understands leading from the front and on the edge. We will soon have a 4-star commander to raise the AutoWarCom flag. And to prepare the way, I am appointing two leaders to guide Project Agincourt during the next year: Owen West and Navy SEAL Senior Chief Max Strasiser. Theirs is going to be a CEO-COO partnership. Owen focused on strategic risk, resources, and scale. And Max focused on operational problem-solving and the realities of employment in combat. Now, this is no theory. It's no one-off. Which is why also today, we are phasing in new MOS frameworks within each Military Department to support our shift to autonomy. We need institutional knowledge and careers paths for a new generation of autonomous warfighters. So today, with Autonomous War Command — AutoWarCom — we institutionalize, and we supercharge, the era of SI, robotics, and autonomous systems. All in order to win. Now next, and second, even as we build the systems on the edge, we need to be thinking even further ahead — years, and decades even into the future, to ensure America's military supremacy. So as we scan that horizon of an unknown future, we should have the humility to recognize that the best forecasters of future conflict do not solely reside inside the Pentagon. There are obvious biases and risks to asking ourselves to both ask the questions and answer them. So today we are leveraging a unique source of American advantage. One our adversaries do not have: our innovators, senior leaders, and technologists — big thinkers and doers who will forecast the creative solutions for tomorrow's conflicts. And that's why today, at my direction, I am announcing Project Meridian, an effort led by America's best minds to study the future of warfare. Under the leadership of the Department's Chief Technology Officer, Emil Michael, Project Meridian will be co-led by three of our nation's best minds: Elon Musk, Palmer Luckey, and Newt Gingrich, all of whom are in the audience with us today. Please stand if you would. Those three great Americans are going be joined by a team of senior leaders hand-picked private sector leaders and subject matter experts from across our nation's unmatched innovation, academic, and policy ecosystems. Project Meridian, the future of warfare, is not about developing new strategies or new policies. We already do that. Rather, its purpose is to creatively look to the future and identify the domains that we must conquer, and capabilities we must master. We should have been thinking about Autonomous Warfare Command ten years ago. We need to be looking forward into the future to achieve technological and military dominance on the battlefield for decades to come. It is futuristic on purpose. Their work will be focused on discovering, developing, and fielding the weapons and systems that our children and our grandchildren will need in their lifetimes without any creative limitations or restrictions. On any future battlefield, from under the Earth to beyond the moon, our American warriors will be armed with absolute technological superiority because we had the foresight to prepare today for tomorrow. And we are going to do so rapidly. That's why I am directing Project Meridian's findings to be completed and submitted within 120 days. Culminating in a full public rollout, of course with a classified annex, to ensure this is not another endless Pentagon study that is outdated before it is finished. In fact, our first meeting with those three great Americans and a small group of us is happening in a SCIF about two hundred yards away right after this speech. We are going to hit the ground running. And in that time, Project Meridian will ruthlessly map the trajectory of war's domains and technologies to ensure this War Department, your War Department, dominates the future. Now, the future is where we will fight, but there we need to maintain what we have in the process and make it impenetrable. For decades we built the most powerful military in the world, and quietly, and regrettably, made it dependent. Dependent on foreign mines for rare earths, on overseas factories for microchips, on foreign supply chains for weapons, and on the civilian power grid to keep the lights on at our bases. Well, that ends today, with my third announcement. Today at my direction we are launching FORTRESS America, a national insurance policy for the American homeland. FORTRESS stands for: Federal Operations for Resilience, Troop Resources, Energy, Supply, and Survivability. And here is what FORTRESS calls for. Every major military installation in America is going to generate its own power. Independent of the civilian grid. If an adversary takes down the grid by cyberattack, by sabotage, by any means, our bases stay lit. Our aircraft keep flying. Our command centers never go dark. We are bringing our critical supply chains home. The rare earths, the specialty metals, the semiconductors, the propellants — mined in America, refined in America, built in America, by American workers. We are building long overdue strategic reserves deep enough to fight through disruption. Think munitions. Fuel. Medicine. Blood. Deep enough that if the world's supply lines break, and in a real war, they are going to break — America keeps fighting anyway. We are hardening every installation on American soil against cyber intrusion, sabotage, and drones. And we are securing the high ground and the airwaves. Our satellites. Our spectrum. Our ability to see, to navigate, and to talk to one another. Previous administrations may have traded away our resilience — one job, one factory, one town, and one base at a time. FORTRESS America is how we get that back. No matter the circumstance, this department will have the power, equipment, and supplies you need to take the fight to the enemy. The Department of War, and the Chairman alluded to this, the Department of War will be the insurance policy for the entire nation. Now insurance is not pessimism. It is what serious people do when the stakes are too high to simply gamble. We are not looking for war, but we will be prepared if one comes. We will make certain that America cannot be starved out, shut down, or cut off. A fortress is not a place where you hide from. It is the ground you stand on. The foundation you fight from. The strength that lets you reach anywhere in the world precisely because you are fully prepared at home. We are going to build FORTRESS America and that starts again today. Now speaking of bases, for too long, and you know this, our military has been bogged down by the same old tired Washington playbook. Spend trillions on exquisite weapons systems, while our troops live in aging bases, outdated barracks, now we are getting after it with the Barracks Task Force, but it is not enough. Outdated barracks and inadequate infrastructure. That era needs to end. Under this Commander-in-Chief's leadership, we are bringing tens of thousands of our finest warriors home from overseas. We are growing our Joint Force by tens of thousands of service members. And we are pivoting our focus to where it belongs, to defending our homeland and our hemisphere while outmatching any global threat. To back up our warfighters, when we bring those troops home, we won't just reshuffle troops onto legacy posts. We are going to build them beautiful new bases from the ground up. That is why today at my direction, the fourth announcement is The Next Great American Base. We haven't built a new base in this country in 40 years. That ends now. President Trump is a builder, and this project is about doing something bold, beautiful, and world-class for the great Americans who wear our Nation's uniform. We are calling on every Governor in the country and every Adjutant General, every TAG, across this country to step up to the plate and bring us their best sales pitch. If your state wants the honor of hosting 15 to 25,000 of America's great troops, show us why and how you are going to do it. Cutting through the red tape, offering up the land, and rolling out the red carpet for our military families. Now this is not going to be a soulless government installation. We will plan out and chart out a dynamic, self-sustaining power projection platform. We are talking hundreds of thousands of acres with organic power generation, modern air defenses, and cutting-edge technology. Think … a FORTRESS. Just as importantly, we are restoring pride and standards to how our troops live. In line with the President's Executive Order on "Beautiful Civic Architecture," this base will be a proud fortress of our Republic, built with timeless, classical architecture. Our soldiers, our Sailors, Airmen, Marines, and Guardians will have clean, first-class barracks, world-class training facilities, and thriving communities with top-tier housing, schools, childcare, and healthcare for families. We owe our warriors nothing less than the gold standard. Now, this entire selection process will be transparent, with the deliberation process recorded for the American people to see. Governors and their TAGs and their leadership teams will come to the Pentagon to pitch their plans to myself, the deputy secretary, and the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. Maybe even the President himself. No backroom Washington deals. No political favoritism. Just a straight-up, merit-based contest to see which state will partner with us to build the most modern, beautiful, and lethal military installation on the planet. And to those states, I say may the best pitch win. Our fifth announcement, like the sixth that will follow, is about people. In an era defined by rapid change and shifting global threats, the demand for grounded, strong, and honorable leaders has never been more urgent. Tomorrow's leaders can't simply manage crises; they have to thrive within in while maintaining their true North compass heading. Only leaders of character, who cherish our Constitution and love our country, should lead our great military. Now thankfully, our military academies at West Point, Annapolis, and Colorado Springs, especially with the new leadership, the new admissions criteria, and new curriculum, they are heading back in the right direction. Back to the basics, from the classroom to field training. These three institutions are critically important because as you know they commission the most officers in our force. The next largest source of future officers is our six existing Senior Military Colleges and their Corps of Cadets. I'm sure many of you attended one of them. Thankfully, the core of these institutions, for the most part, have not wavered. I had a chance to see a great one at Texas A&M a couple of weeks ago. In fact, places like that have doubled down on American values. The patriotic and selfless service being taught at places like Texas A&M, VMI, the Citadel, Norwich, Virginia Tech, and the University of North Georgia are exactly what our Nation needs. But after that, we rely on a wide variety of commissioning sources. Many from institutions that have drifted, in some cases, have careened away from founding values. Now, I don't need to give a sermon about the failings of higher education. You get it. I once wrote a book about it. From the Ivy Leagues to most liberal arts colleges, our colleges and universities have become anti-American, DEI-worshiping, woke factories. Qualities like grit and courage were replaced with political correctness and social justice. God and country traded for Che Guevara and critical theory. What do we need? We need students of Western Civilization and the pillars of our Republic. Leaders who understand the faith of Jerusalem, the philosophy of Athens, the power of Rome, and the freedom of Philadelphia, circa 1776. Officers of the Republic, proud of our country, proud of our heritage, and proud of our history and those who serve it. We need more officers from academic institutions like our Military Academies and Senior Military Colleges. And today, we are going to make that happen. Enter a new Corp of Cadets. To meet this critical need, we are partnering with a new crop of premier higher-ed institutions, including Louisiana State University, LSU, Liberty University, Tuskegee University, Mississippi State University, and Hillsdale College. These schools have stepped forward to answer the call to duty and establish new Corps of Cadets in partnership with the Department of War. So, today at my direction, we are formally establishing a program to assist these universities and colleges. It is called America's Corps of Cadets. This flagship effort is central to our goal of increasing the number of patriotic leaders of character who are commissioned into our Joint Force. Each member school is designated a "Distinguished Military College," reviving a category previously used in our department. And in this status, these institutions maintain exceptionally high standards of cadet discipline, tactical instruction, and military organization. Additionally, these schools earn a prestigious "Honor School" status, which grants priority in officer commissioning, which you all know is a big deal. We are grateful to these initial five institutions for stepping forward and there are a number more that we plan to announce soon. The status quo of our officer pipeline is pretty good. But the future will be even better. By embedding continuous military discipline and leadership development into new institutions, by growing our Corps of Cadets, the War Department will ensure our Republic is defended by even more officers of unwavering character and patriotism. Finally, cutting edge technology, which we talked about, new basing and bases, which we talked about, and a better educational pipeline are still incomplete without the most essential component of our Republic: faith. Faith in something greater than us. When an American warrior raises their right hand to defend our Nation, you sign away a lot more than just time. You miss births, you miss first steps, you miss final goodbyes. You miss other civilian careers. But one of the costs that is rarely thought about or talked about is the loss of your religious community. Every time we issue orders to move a warrior to a new location, they leave behind the faith community, the church that grounds them. For people of faith, that community isn't just a "nice to have." In many ways, it's an extension of their family. It's their moral foundation or their personal and spiritual accountability. The very bedrock of their warrior ethos. When you actually look at the numbers, and this will be good for the press, less than 5% of our force identifies as non-religious. Less than 5%. Meaning, 95% of our force recognizes an Almighty God. Accordingly, our department therefore has a sacred duty — first-class religious support wherever we send our warriors. Now for far too long, you know, we didn't prioritize that duty at all. It was an afterthought. Political correctness and secular humanism got a vote — chaplains did not. Budgets were cut. Resourcing and manpower needs were ignored. Base chapels fell apart. Decisions about faith and religion were made by secular careerists in cubicles and lawyers running around with red tape. We don't put non-lawyers in charge of our JAG Corps. Or non-doctors in charge of our military surgeons. Yet for decades, we let people with no expertise in faith or religion dictate the spiritual life of our warriors. The people who actually practice faith and religion, our chaplains, were buried echelons deep, waiting for permission. We asked chaplains to serve and sacrifice and then sidelined them with paperwork and process. And that ends now. Today, at my direction, I am establishing the Office of Religious Affairs. Starting today, and for Secretaries of War after me, the Office of Religious Affairs will report straight to the top. No staff filters . No bureaucratic dilution. A direct line to the Secretary. This won't be a paper pushing shop. It will have real teeth. It will protect budgets, demand infrastructure, and strengthen religious support. The experts, our chaplains, will finally have an advocate at the highest levels. Policy and resources will serve the mission, not smother the mission. As Psalm 33:12 extols us: "Blessed is the Nation whose God is the Lord." Two hundred and fifty years ago we rejected an earthly King an ocean away, appealing instead to a Heavenly King above. George Washington made sure the Continental Army had chaplains back at the beginning, back in 1775. That force appealed to Heaven, and we still do today. Our national motto is, after all "in God we Trust." Today we reaffirm that trust. We are placing spiritual health at the same level as physical health. Our department is, you might say, is putting on the full Armor of God. Because while we wage physical war, we all know the real battle is spiritual. God is good. Evil is not. America's military must understand the difference. To our incredible chaplains and religious support teams, live your calling. Stand firm. Preach Truth. Minister to the Flock. Fear no man. Or, as the Psalmist put it, "The Lord is on my side; I will not fear: What can man do unto me?" Amen to that. So six Announcements, all charting the course for our department. Autonomous Warfare. The Future of Warfare. The Nation's Insurance Policy. The Next Great American Base. A new Corps of Cadets. And the Office of Religious Affairs. All for you. Each of you swore an oath to the Constitution ending with "So Help me God." And when I raised my right hand in this job, and made that same solemn pledge, we sealed a shared covenant. Up to and including the price of the lives of our best Americans. Our absolute best. Each of us committed to the Nation with the sentiment of the sixth chapter of the Book of Isaiah: "Lord, here I am, send me." Send me to fight the Red Coats. Send me to fight the Communists. Send me to fight the Islamists. Send me. See, the Ivy League faculty lounges, they'll never understand you, and that's okay, because they could never, ever do what you do. The media will mischaracterize you, and that's okay. Because deep down they know you're the real reason they live free. They envy you because you do real things every single day. You are the real 1%. In the middle of the Profession of Arms. You feel comfortable inside the violence so that our citizens can live peacefully. Lethality is your calling card and victory your only acceptable end-state. The outside world can't understand this, so stay true to this department. You don't want to look like civilians, because you are different, you are set apart. You are warriors. With that title comes great expectations. So go forth this day and do good things. Do hard things. President Trump has your back, and so do I. We are the War Department. And we will never back down. Godspeed. Thank you very much.

title: Statement by Chief Pentagon Spokesman Sean Parnell on the Conclusion of the U.S. Military Mission in Iraq
text: Today, the United States and our Coalition partners formally concluded Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq, consistent with the September 2024 U.S.-Iraq joint statement and U.S. national interests. The orderly departure of Coalition forces and equipment from Erbil Air Base marks the successful conclusion of the military mission that defeated ISIS in Iraq. This milestone reflects the success of a 12-year campaign that defeated ISIS as an organized military threat in Iraq and across the region. It also marks a transition from a wartime coalition mission to an Iraqi-led security effort supported by a more normal bilateral security relationship. We expect the Iraqi Security Forces, including the Peshmerga and other security forces in the Iraqi Kurdistan Region, to lead the continuing effort to secure Iraq and keep ISIS remnants suppressed. The Department of War will continue to provide targeted training and intelligence support to our Iraqi partners. The primary responsibility for addressing Iraq's remaining security challenges, including ISIS remnants and Iran-aligned militias that undermine Iraqi sovereignty and regional stability, now rests with the Government of Iraq. The United States remains committed to counterterrorism and will continue to work with Iraq and our partners to ensure ISIS can never reconstitute from Iraqi territory. The United States supports a strong sovereign Iraq that secures its borders, protects its people, and serves as the foundation for deeper commercial, diplomatic, and security cooperation between our two countries.

title: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth Signs Directive to Defend 2026 Elections From Foreign Threats
text: In direct support of President Donald J. Trump's commitment to election integrity, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has signed a memorandum directing the Department of War to mobilize a comprehensive, whole-of-government defense of our election infrastructure from foreign adversaries. Under the Secretary's directive, U.S. Cyber Command and Combat Support Agencies will prioritize and deploy advanced intelligence and cyber capabilities to identify, disrupt, and neutralize foreign interference in U.S. democratic processes. "Free and fair elections are the foundation of our republic," said Chief Pentagon Spokesman Sean Parnell. "By working in lockstep with federal, state, and local partners, U.S. Cyber Command and our defense intelligence teams will defend the integrity of America's voting systems, expose foreign malign influence, and ensure our democratic processes remain secure from external manipulation while protecting the fundamental freedoms of the American people." "U.S. Cyber Command and the National Security Agency are closely partnered to identify and defend against cyber threats to our nation. The Command and the Agency regularly counter actions by malicious foreign cyber actors including those with the intent to interfere with our democratic process," said Gen. Joshua M. Rudd, commander, U.S. Cyber Command and director of the National Security Agency/chief, CSS. The Department will effectively wield its capabilities to protect and uphold the reliability of America's voting mechanisms against external manipulation and disruption from foreign actors, while maintaining the fundamental freedoms that characterize our country. Click here to read the memo.

title: Remarks by Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby to NATO's North Atlantic Council (As Prepared)
text: Good afternoon. Thank you for that kind introduction. It is an honor to be back here at NATO Headquarters. Thank you to Secretary General Rutte for his generous hospitality. My visit here today is designed to both speak to and hear from you about our important Europe Posture Review, which Secretary Hegseth announced at the last defense ministerial in June. We are now in the midst of that review. On Tuesday, I had the opportunity to visit U.S. European Command, where much of the analysis is being done. Yesterday, I also had the opportunity to visit Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe and hear from General Grynkewich and his staff there. Both visits were exceedingly productive. My purpose today is to give you, our allies, a clear sense of our strategic and overall approach in this important initiative and then invite your feedback, building on conversations already underway among many of our teams. To begin with, I hope and believe that we have been clear and consistent in our approach towards deterrence and defense with our NATO allies. Fundamentally, we believe that in order to survive and indeed thrive, NATO must change. The simple fact is that the legacy model of NATO 2.0 is no longer suited for our time. Instead, NATO must adapt. We term this NATO 3.0: restoring an alliance grounded in flexible realism; focused on warfighting readiness; and designed to deter, defend, and sustain peace in the North Atlantic area—even under conditions of simultaneity, with our allies taking primary responsibility for Europe's conventional defense. To be sure, not everyone agreed with this need for change and that approach. But I believe we can all be proud to say that we have made tremendous progress over the last 18 months in coming to a broad consensus on the need for NATO 3.0. Thanks to President Trump and key leaders like Secretary General Rutte, both the United States and Europe essentially now agree on this critical point: we must make NATO more focused on warfighting readiness, more balanced, and more pragmatic. This is not a transient view, but rather a structural and strategic necessity, particularly in light of the simultaneity problem. Moreover, it not only benefits the American people by making NATO more balanced, it is also to Europe's benefit because it will make the alliance more sustainable and durable. Among almost all NATO allies, the conversation has now turned from whether this needs to happen to how best to make NATO 3.0 a reality and how to do so most rapidly and effectively. This is exactly where the conversation should be, concentrating in matters of timing, force development, budget allocation, and managing risk. This is the kind of pragmatic, strategic, realistic conversation that needs to happen, and represents a fundamental and welcome shift from the almost-theological focus that characterized the transatlantic relationship until very recently. Indeed, I think it can be said plainly that it represents enormous progress from where the discussion was just two years ago, progress that seemed impossible to some but has since come to pass. For this we should take satisfaction. But we cannot rest on our laurels. Coming to a shared perception that NATO needs to adapt to the NATO 3.0 model is vital, but this is only a beginning. It represents a recognition of our need to adapt — but is not the adaptation itself. It is in that spirit that we have embarked on a review of U.S. force posture and basing in Europe at Secretary Hegseth's direction. As he laid out in June, this will be a real review, "designed to ensure that NATO is moving fast and irreversibly toward Europe leading, stepping up to take primary responsibility for the defense of Europe, stepping up to ensure our forces are postured for America's global needs, and making sure that our access, basing, and overflight are clearly delineated and assured." At the Secretary's direction, I am leading this review in close coordination and deep collaboration with General Grynkewich. Allow me to stress a few things about how we are approaching this review. First and foremost, we are proceeding in a spirit of flexible realism and strategic rigor, as you will have seen in the Terms of Reference distributed to your capitals at the beginning of this effort. Second, we are doing so to advance and accelerate NATO 3.0, to make the alliance more fit for the times and for the strategic requirements that the United States as well as our allies face. In this vein, over the last few weeks, our teams have been working hard to think strategically, broadly, and rigorously about how to adapt America's strategic posture in Europe for the age in which we find ourselves and going forward. This is not a narrow review about places and bases alone, although those are of course important. Rather, it is a look at our strategic posture here in the broader sense, designed to enable our Joint Force to meet the priorities laid out in the National Security Strategy and the National Defense Strategy. It will encourage, enable, and impel a transition to a more durable and powerful European-led conventional defense of the continent, consistent with NATO's original and noble purpose. That is, the goal is for Europeans to be partners, not dependencies—not just, I stress, for our sake but for yours as well, so that NATO can always reliably defend Europe effectively, even in the most stressing scenarios. In this effort, we have no preconceived fixed goal or outcome. There are several starting points from which we proceeded, however: the priorities of our nation as laid out in our canonical Strategies are on the Western Hemisphere and the First Island Chain, even as Europe remains a critical area for the United States and the NATO alliance a key part of European and Atlantic security. We also know that our European allies can step up to assume primary responsibility for their own conventional defense and have made historic commitments to make that a reality, which will enable the Alliance to defend Europe effectively even in the case of simultaneous contingencies. We also know that our allies can and will lead in supporting Ukraine's self-defense, and that this is highly consonant with Ukraine's own battlefield successes. At the same time, we know that a significant portion of U.S. force posture in Europe derives from the Cold War era. Further, we know that Europe is not only important but also provides a critical node for the projection of U.S. military power on all our behalf, both in this theater and beyond, and helps contribute to the defense of the U.S. homeland. These are the kinds of factors which we are incorporating into our analysis. Allow me to stress another critical point: consultations and engagement are a vital part of this review. As evidenced by my visit here this week, we are not trying to hide what we are doing. Obviously, we cannot get into every detail, but I submit that we are being clear, candid, and consistent in our strategic approach. Moreover, we want to hear from you. In this setting as well as throughout this week, my colleagues and I have been meeting with both civilian and uniformed leaders from our European allies. I also have been having meetings in Washington, and for those who have not yet had the chance, I invite you to come visit the Pentagon where we can discuss things more deeply. But we are not relying solely on snippets and conversations. This is why we have sent out a detailed questionnaire to all of you earlier this month. The logic behind this is to ensure that we hear directly from our allies in formal, written responses. As you know, the thrust of that questionnaire is all about NATO 3.0. It is about understanding how all of you are thinking about moving towards that noble goal that almost all of us share. It was sent in a spirit of candor, directness, and clarity, with a clear eye toward the most important things that we can do to advance this goal of a stronger, more sustainable Alliance. We look forward to receiving responses from all of you and we appreciate those who have already sent ones. All responses will be incorporated into our work. Allow me to close by stressing that together, we find ourselves with an historic opportunity, which we should not miss. Thanks to the leadership of President Trump, Secretary General Rutte, and many of your national leaders, we have broken with the tired and ill-suited shibboleths of NATO 2.0 and come to a common agreement that European allies must take primary responsibility for their own conventional defense and meet the historic Hague defense spending commitments made last year. I simply cannot stress enough how significant this shift is, and candidly, I do not believe we pay enough attention to how dramatic our progress so far has been. While we should not slip into a false sense of complacency on this point – indeed, a great deal of the real work still lies ahead of us – I also believe we should recognize the significance of what has happened and the historic opportunity it provides. After a generation of disarmament and functional demilitarization, many countries in Europe, including several of Europe's largest and most advanced economies, are rebuilding their military strength for collective defense. They are making real sacrifices, some even going so far as to change their constitutions and raising their retirement age. That is extraordinary. Accordingly, we must not waste this opportunity. Now is the time, when the concrete is still wet, to set the trajectory for the coming decade and beyond, to make the best use of that extraordinary shift brought about by President Trump and key European leaders. Our approach, and this review, are designed to accelerate and build on this. To be clear, this does not mean a return to an idle reassurance of the past. Rather, it means looking with clear eyes and strategic realism at the geopolitical and military situation that we face here in the North Atlantic and European areas, but also for us Americans around the globe, especially in our own hemisphere and along the First Island Chain. If we work together in this vein, I have every hope that we will advance the vision of NATO 3.0 together and put this historic alliance on a stronger and more durable footing for the next generation and beyond. Thank you very much.

title: Department of War Announces a $750 Million Investment as Part of a $1.55 Billion Initiative to Secure Critical Rare-Earth Elements From Serra Verde
text: The Department of War's (DoW) Economic Defense Unit (EDU), in partnership with the Office of the Assistant Secretary of War for Industrial Base Policy (IBP) announced today a $750 million investment with US SIIE, LLC through the Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment (IBAS) program. These funds will be utilized to support an offtake agreement for mixed rare-earth carbonates (MREC) produced at Serra Verde's Pela Ema Project in central Brazil. This strategic partnership will establish a secure supply chain for rare-earth elements (REE) critical for national defense and economic security. This $750 million is part of a broader $1.55 billion total investment structure mobilized by EDU, which includes a $300 million purchase commitment from the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) and a $500 million commitment from a money-center bank. "Securing resilient domestic and allied supply chains is a fundamental warfighting requirement," said HON Mike Cadenazzi, Assistant Secretary of War for Industrial Base Policy. "By partnering with Serra Verde, we are taking a decisive step to break our adversaries' near-monopoly on rare-earth elements. This collaborative effort ensures that our defense industrial base has the guaranteed, long-term access to the critical materials needed to manufacture next-generation weapons systems and maintain our technological edge." This initiative aggressively addresses an over-dependence on China for rare-earth elements. Once fully operational, this project will secure a massive supply of vital elements like Dysprosium, Terbium, Neodymium, and Praseodymium, effectively bypassing Chinese supply chain dominance and supporting emerging U.S. magnet manufacturing capabilities. The deal follows a DFC financing agreement with Serra Verde for a $565 million loan to optimize and expand the Pela Ema Project. These investments work in parallel with the Department of Commerce's efforts to establish a non-Chinese mine-to-magnet value chain. "This historic $1.55 billion investment is a major step towards securing one of the most vital supply chains for our warfighters and our economy," said George K. Kollitides II, Director of the Economic Defense Unit. "By ensuring reliable access to these critical rare-earth elements, we are protecting the production of everything from fighter jets and nuclear submarines to the energy infrastructure and commercial technology that power our modern world." Rare-earth elements are necessary to improve the thermal stability and magnetic strength of Neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) magnets, which are essential for manufacturing critical components for our warfighters. These include advanced systems in nuclear submarines, fighter jets, satellites, guided missiles, combat vessels, and drones. Beyond defense, these high-purity materials are a vital raw material for energy infrastructure, transportation, aerospace, and electronics, making them a cornerstone of a modern, industrial economy.

title: Department of War Releases Its Fiscal Year 2025 Annual Report on Sexual Assault in the Military
text: The Department of War released its Fiscal Year 2025 Annual Report on Sexual Assault in the Military today. The Department remains committed to preventing sexual assault and sexual harassment, and continues to confront and counter harmful behaviors, provide victim assistance, and strengthen command climates. "Dignity, respect, and discipline are foundational to the warrior ethos and the overall preparedness of the force. Sexual assault and sexual harassment undermine these values, eroding trust and threatening the mission," said Under Secretary of War for Personnel and Readiness Anthony J. Tata. "The FY 2025 report underscores our ongoing commitment to maintaining high standards, protecting our people, and building a unified, ready, and lethal fighting force," added Tata. Required by Congress, the Annual Report on Sexual Assault in the Military presents critical statistics, trend analyses, and updates on the Department’s ongoing efforts to prevent and respond to sexual assault and sexual harassment in the military. The FY 2025 report incorporates findings from the 2025 Workplace Experiences Survey – a congressionally mandated assessment measuring the prevalence of unwanted sexual contact, sexual harassment, and sex discrimination across the force. It shows that the prevalence of unwanted sexual contact among active-duty Service members decreased from FY 2023 – the last time that the Workplace Experiences Survey was administered – to FY 2025. The estimated rate of unwanted sexual contact for active-duty men decreased from 1.3% to 1.0% and the estimated rate of unwanted sexual contact for active-duty women decreased from 6.8% to 4.3%. Based on these rates, the Department estimates that 20,492 Service members experienced some form of unwanted sexual contact in FY 2025, which is 8,500 fewer personnel compared to FY 2023. Likewise, the FY 2025 report shows that the prevalence of sexual harassment within the active-duty force decreased between FY 2023 and FY 2025. The estimated rate of sexual harassment for active-duty men decreased from 5.8% to 4.4% and the estimated rate of sexual harassment for active-duty women decreased from 24.7% to 17.5%. Finally, the FY 2025 report shows that reporting of sexual assault incidents by active-duty Service members increased from 25% in FY 2023 to 33% in FY 2025. The Department continues to encourage greater reporting to connect warfighters with vital restorative care and enable leadership to hold offenders appropriately accountable. The Department remains focused on strengthening prevention and response activities and ensuring that Service members can operate with confidence and maintain absolute focus on the mission. The FY 2025 Annual Report on Sexual Assault in the Military is available at https://www.sapr.mil/ .

title: Department of War Orders Research Security Audits at 30 Academic Institutions
text: The Department of War has issued formal notifications to 30 domestic academic institutions, directing them to initiate immediate and comprehensive reviews of their academic, financial and research collaborations with foreign entities of concern. These notifications address active institutional ties and collaborations with foreign entities identified under Section 1286 of the FY19 NDAA, as well as organizations associated with rebranded Confucius Institutes. Executed by the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering, this action is designed to protect American taxpayer-funded research investments from unauthorized technology transfer, intellectual property theft and adversarial exploitation. "The Department of War has zero tolerance for academic partnerships that compromise our national security," said Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering. "Institutions that receive funding from American taxpayers must uphold the highest standards of research security, and these mandated audits will ensure accountability across the board." To maintain eligibility for future federal research funding, the notified universities must complete a comprehensive audit of all identified foreign collaborations, assess the exposure of sensitive or export-controlled research, and implement strict mitigation plans, including the termination of problematic partnerships. Institutions are required to report their findings and actions directly to the Department no later than August 31, 2026. "Universities are critical partners in executing a wide range of Department of War research programs, and the Department must therefore ensure that our research investments are well protected from foreign exploitation," said Dr. Joseph Jewell, Assistant Secretary of War for Science and Technology. Through these audits, the Department of War will better anticipate emerging threats, adapt to evolving adversarial tactics and maintain America's position as a global leader in innovation. The Department is pursuing this effort alongside partners in Congress. Together with the House and Senate Armed Services Committees, the House and Senate Appropriations Committees and the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, the Department continues to build a robust research ecosystem that protects critical discoveries from exploitation.

title: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth Delivers Remarks at the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition Conference in Panama (As Delivered)
text: SECRETARY OF WAR PETE HEGSETH: Well, general, thank you very much for that update. And, today is the end of a conference forum here that was meant to be and has been operational and productive. Focused on what we can do together. So, I want to thank the president of Panama, I want to thank Minister Abrego, I want to thank all of our Panamanian partners for being such great hosts here. And for PANAMAX, which is ongoing for the first time in 14 years, live here in Panama, thousands of troops right now from many of the nations represented here. And I want to thank every single country. Sovereign, strong country, willing to step up and address this threat as a part of the America's Counter Cartel Coalition. But before we begin, just a moment, as the Senator did, to offer my sympathy to the people of Colombia for the — for Monday's devastating earthquake that I understand was even felt here in Panama. And the Department of War, with the State Department, is mobilizing critical life-saving aid to support the Colombian government's robust response to this tragic event, just as we did in Venezuela a few weeks ago. I also want to thank my team as well, chief — Senator Moreno, thank you for representing not only the United States of America, but this hemisphere so effectively, and being such a powerful voice in the Senate for this effort as well. I'm grateful to be here with ministers and Chiefs of Defense, united in purpose and resolve as partners in the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition, or ACCC. Just a few months ago, we laid out a shared vision for a safe, secure Western hemisphere where borders and laws are respected, and narco terrorists are brought to swift and absolute justice. And yesterday and today, and going forward, we are gathered to take the next step in our shared fight against narco-terrorists, gang members, and drug and human traffickers – designated terrorist organizations, the ISIS and al Qaeda of the Western Hemisphere, no different and they should be treated as such. It's now nearly one year since the launch of Operation Southern Spear, the first time in history that the Department of War launched a sustained military campaign against US designated terrorist organizations in our shared hemisphere. And it has been a resounding success thus far. We've seen record drops in movements of narco vessels across major maritime corridors inside our hemisphere. Including, at a minimum, 65 percent reduction in the western Caribbean, a 60 percent reduction in the eastern Caribbean, and a nearly 50 percent reduction in the eastern Pacific in the north and south of the Galapagos Islands. We have knocked the narco-terrorists in the maritime domain on their heels. We forced them to adjust their tactics, techniques and procedures, their TTPs, and operate outside of their comfort zones. We are retaking the open seas and our maritime borders. This is a bad time to get in a drug boat in the Western Hemisphere. The results are historic, the United States — in the United States: fatal drug overdoses have dropped dramatically; flows of fentanyl are way down; crossings at our southwest border have dropped to zero; the murder rate in American cities is at modern all-time lows, historic drops in crime. Life-changing progress that benefits each and every citizen of the United States of America, and indeed, every citizen of your nations as well. Now, predictably, as we like to call them, the fake news media has tried to discredit and delegitimize Operation Southern Spear. These same voices said nothing when governments allowed an unprecedented border crisis and record drug overdoses and deaths. Yet now they deny, and try to diminish, our success — our shared success. The left-wing media wants us to return to the failed strategies of the past, when America neglected our own neighborhood and our own neighborhoods. Even as we sent our best, in our case American troops, to do nation building halfway across the world. Globalists in Washington looked the other way while our friends and neighbors to our South were victimized by drugs, violence, mass migration, Marxism, and foreign exploitation. The Biden administration and the Democrats ignored the US southern border, openly accepting mass illegal immigration and destroying many of our great American cities — an invasion, no doubt. Under decades of globalist neglect more than 1 million Americans died from fentanyl, cocaine and other drugs. That's more loss than the United States had suffered in any war in our 250-year history. This blatant neglect for our national security also destroyed your borders and your sovereignty and your immigration systems as well. That is why we're here today together. Now, to be fair, I understand you may be feeling, and your countries may be feeling, and your militaries may be feeling some whiplash. Because just 18 months ago, the previous US administration under Joe Biden, especially the previous administration here at Southern Command, stood in front of you promoting priorities like gender issues, women, peace and security, or climate change or diversity — dudes in dresses. I've said this before, but the Department of War is done with that nonsense, full stop. And I assume you and your countries are as well. Real threats, real capabilities, no more leftist make believe or dress up time. The hard-working, law-abiding people of our nations suffered together far too long. But now we are working together, we are building together and we are training together. We are killing terrorists. And we're defeating the failed and toxic ideologies of radical socialism and communism. Now, speaking of socialism, make no doubt about it, the international left, along with their enabling left-wing media, is plotting to unlawfully assert International Criminal Court jurisdiction over US and partner military personnel and operations. To be clear, there is no legitimate basis for the ICC's lawless power grab that they will entertain anywhere they can in the world. Our efforts in this effort are 100 percent lawful under the laws of armed conflict. It's striking that this so-called court and other globalist bodies undermine our efforts but do nothing to hold real terrorists and real tyrants accountable. And that's why the ICC poses a threat to your national sovereignty, your constitutional mandates, and the national interests of your people — just as it does ours. Our nations retain our sovereignty, and our ability to deploy our own warriors in our own defense. We will never relinquish our absolute right to defend ourselves from threats to our safeties and our citizens of my country and of your countries. We answer only to our own citizens and our own constitutions, not unelected international bureaucrats. That's why I strongly encourage every ACCC member to leave the ICC, and reject their attempts to rob your governments and your courts of your sovereignty. I know as a soldier, I swore an oath to the Constitution, not some fake and illegitimate international court. And in these efforts, we've already shown that deterrence works. Operation Southern Spear is a model that can be and should be followed across our hemisphere by each of you to degrade, dismantle, and destroy narco terrorist networks. Under the leadership of General Donovan, the success of Operation Southern Spear will be transferred to the newly established Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere, the action arm of US Southern Command, to continue the targeting and killing of narco-terrorists that threaten our shared backyard. I want to commend Ecuador for its regional leadership to become the first ACCC member to partner with the United States in combined kinetic operation against narco-terrorists in Ecuador. I also want to commend Honduras and Guatemala for inviting the United States to partake in combined operations against narco-terrorists in their countries. Your people are already safer and more free for your courage and your resolve, and we look forward to working with you in killing bad guys. Additionally, I want to thank Jamaica for working with the Department of War to create a new military partnership to cripple narco-terrorists that transit through the Caribbean. This partnership will forever change the security environment of the Caribbean. And finally, I'm also proud to announce that Colombia will join the ACCC, becoming the 19th member. And through the newly inaugurated president, as our president likes to say, President El Tigre, Colombia has already requested the Department of War join Colombia in its fight against narco-terrorism, authorizing joint military operations to destroy terrorists and terror networks. Thank you very much. Aggressive and concrete steps like these exemplify the types of active participation, operationally focused, we want to see from our partners that will make the ACCC a potent and lethal coalition. Yes, we have meetings; yes, we will coordinate; but ultimately this is about the operations we can conduct together jointly to protect individual sovereignty and the entirety of the hemisphere. The Trump administration knows that a safer backyard means a safer home. You can't have prosperity without security. In fact, eventually, economic security taking hold is the long-term solution, but you need physical security to enable that economic security. With you, with all of you, the United States will forge a safe, stable, and prosperous Western Hemisphere. We seek neither domination nor dependency, we only seek — and I know you feel this from SOUTHCOM and from the general — genuine partnership with your governments to achieve security, stability and prosperity. Two centuries ago, the Monroe Doctrine was America's first standing — first stand against foreign meddling and exploitation in our hemisphere. The United States declared to European colonial powers that we will regard any threat against the free nations of this hemisphere as a threat to the United States itself. Well, now, under President Trump's strong, clear, and visionary leadership, we follow the Trump corollary to the Monroe Doctrine. We will defend our hemisphere from external threats to national sovereignty, whether from narco-terrorism or foreign malign actors. And we will deny adversaries the ability to position forces, or otherwise threaten capabilities, in our hemisphere. And that's why the United States is particularly grateful for the strong leadership in Panama of President José Raúl Mulino, right here. It's my second time to Panama and the strides that we have made together over the last year, I think, are exemplary of the type of partnership we look for in this hemisphere. President Mulino has courageously rejected foreign malign coercion and boldly resisted international pressure tactics. Panama has set a strong example for rejecting threats to their sovereignty, threats to the Panama Canal and, instead, advancing US partnership on both. And with Panama and other countries, the United States will continue to lead the way. Under President Trump, the United States War Department seeks a historic, generational investment in our military spending through a new $1.5 trillion budget. We have work to do with our Congress but, make no mistake, we will work as hard as humanly possible with Republicans and across the aisle, if we can, to deliver what is truly a necessary historic investment to ensure America remains the dominant military power on planet earth. Thankfully, US allies and NATO likewise have vastly increased their commitment to the common defense. And we believe that ACCC members must follow this example as well. The Department of War is willing and able to support all of you to enhance your military capabilities. But, of course, we expect substantial investment in your own abilities as well and for those to be increased on defense resources. If countries are serious about their defense, the Department of War will prioritize our efforts to enhance your capabilities and fight beside you on the battlefield. And, to reiterate, not really necessary for this group, but around the globe, President Trump does not tolerate free riding, and there are no — we're not here for games. When we say we will dismantle the cartels, we mean it. And I know the nations of this coalition feel the exact same way on behalf of their citizens. And will take concrete steps, sometimes risky steps, courageous steps in partnership, such as reaching status of forces agreements or access basing and overflight agreements. Our citizens and our nations deserve and expect real, concrete actions. We believe there's no time to waste and no better time than right now. And we will be with you, I pledge to you, from the White House to the Pentagon, shoulder to shoulder, every step of the way. Because, together, we are the offspring of Western civilization. Our nations are, and will always be united by heritage, history, and geography in this new world. We share the same interests and the same civilizational soul. And so, we all face the same essential test — whether our nations will remain western nations, remain prosperous nations, remain Christian nations under God, remain proud of our shared heritage with strong borders and prosperous people — ruled not by violence and chaos, but by law and order. Or instead, whether we are permanently torn apart by something else – narco-terrorists, violence, radical Marxism and globalist exploitation, social denigration, and so-called social justice. We've had great collaboration in recent months. And I want to thank each and every one of you for supporting our ability to find, fix and finish narco-terrorist targets. Ultimately, that is what it is going to require — finding, fixing, and finishing narco-terrorists either unilaterally — unilaterally or bilaterally, by, with and through and together, finding, fixing and finishing narco-terrorists. And we'll finish the job, which is why I'm proud to announce the new motto of the ACCC —maybe formal, maybe informal, I haven't decided yet. The new motto of the ACCC is we do bad things to bad people. That's the mentality I want to have inside this room. Now we're good people that do good things. But ultimately, we're dealing with bad people that have done a lot of bad things to a lot of good people for a very long time. And they're about to meet a new sheriff in town in the ACCC, and we mean business. Narco-terrorists, DTOs, drug traffickers are hereby on notice. Under President Trump we will make the Americas great again. The safety and prosperity of one will strengthen the safety and prosperity of all. God bless you, and God bless the great citizens of your countries. Thank you very much.

title: The Department of War Releases Updated List of Foreign Institutions Engaging in Problematic Activities to Counter Unauthorized Technology Transfer
text: The Department of War today announced the publication of the Fiscal Year (FY) 2025 update to the list of foreign institutions engaging in problematic activities, as required by Section 1286 of the FY19 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). This update is a vital component of the Department's ongoing mission to highlight and counter unauthorized technology transfer to foreign countries of concern. The FY25 list formally identifies 130 academic and research institutions located in China, Russia and Iran. These institutions have been confirmed to engage in activities that increase the likelihood of U.S. government-funded research and development efforts being misappropriated. Such misappropriation enables adversarial government interference that directly threatens America's national security and scientific integrity. "The Department of War is strengthening its commitment to protect taxpayer-funded research and preserving the integrity of the American scientific enterprise," said Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering.
